request: We had the monthly spending and then the yearly total. Now put the two together: how the same 2025 spending adds up over the year.

plan.title: Spending adding up over 2025
plan.question: Spending of 2025 added up from January onwards, the running total after each month, one row per month, columns month as 'YYYY-MM' and cumulative_eur.

sql:
WITH per_month AS (
  SELECT strftime('%Y-%m', booked_on) AS month, -SUM(amount) AS spent

request: First the August gap, then September. Draw the step from one month to the next across 2025: which months rose against the one before them and which fell.

plan.title: Change to the month before
plan.question: For each month of 2025 from February onwards the difference between what was spent in it and what was spent the month before, signed so that a cheaper month is negative, one row per month, columns month as 'YYYY-MM' and change_eur.

sql:
WITH per_month AS (
  SELECT strftime('%Y-%m', booked_on) AS month, -SUM(amount_cents) AS spent
  FROM transaction_view
  WHERE amount < 0
  GROUP BY month
)
SELECT month, ROUND(spent - LAG(spent) OVER (ORDER BY month), 2) AS change_eur
FROM per_month
WHERE month > '2025-01'
ORDER BY month
reasoning_plan:

the two earlier turns named single months of 2025
'more or less than' is a signed difference, so plain bars above and below zero
the figure is summed from amount_cents, so it is a hundred times the euro amount
the columns are month and change_eur, the euro column last
reasoning_code:
the shape is bar, so the mark is barY and the bars stay thin
the columns are month and change_eur, and change_eur holds the numbers, signed
months on x on a band scale with monthShort, euros on y
a bar rests on zero itself, so the euro axis is the bare scaleLinear factory and the negative months hang below it
